name: set_slot_flag_clear_word
description: Sets the high bit of a status byte in a 32-byte slot record, chosen by the index in the data register, then clears the longword that follows it. The routine has no callers other than one unnamed routine.

name: reserve_and_fill_sector_buffer
description: Reserves a region sized in 512-byte blocks for a slot record, then copies staged data in 512-byte pieces when the source and target sizes match, otherwise calling a transfer subroutine. It marks the slot as ready and clears its pending counter when it finishes.

name: dispatch_unrecovered_jump_table
description: Calls one subroutine and then performs an indirect call through a jump table the decompiler could not recover, so the real target is unknown.

name: decode_control_bit_stream
description: Expands a packed input in which each control byte supplies eight flags: a set flag emits the byte from a lookup indexed by the previous output byte, and a clear flag copies the next literal input byte. Decoding stops when the requested number of output bytes has been produced.

name: setup_trap_and_run_init
description: Installs a trap handler address, clears a low-memory vector area, copies a block of code to a second location, and unpacks length-prefixed byte runs. It then calls setup subroutines in sequence and enters an endless loop that doubles and subtracts a counter while waiting.

name: disable_interrupts_then_init_system
description: Writes the interrupt-enable mask with bit 15 clear to disable all interrupts, clears a low-memory vector area, and copies a block of code into place. It unpacks length-prefixed byte runs, sets the copper list pointer, calls setup subroutines and then enters an endless loop.

name: restart_copper_after_raster_wait
description: If a pending flag is set, clears it, runs four subroutines, and waits in a loop until a counter reaches a fixed value. It then stores a copper-list address and clears a word before returning. The copper, DMA and vertical-position registers are involved.

name: poll_flag_table_then_clear
description: Its opening test is always true, so the code shown returns at once and the wait-and-clear logic after it is never reached. The intended behaviour was to wait for a flag and then zero a table of 32 longwords.

name: run_main_wait_loop
description: Calls several subroutines, zeroes a counter, and then loops indefinitely, doubling and subtracting the counter while calling subroutines and waiting on its value.

name: advance_counter_run_six_steps
description: Increments a shared counter and then calls six subroutines in sequence. It has no other logic.

name: advance_lfsr_state_eight_steps
description: Advances a 32-bit shared state eight times, shifting it left and XORing in a fixed feedback constant when the shifted-out bit or a zero result requires it. This is a linear feedback shift update, the usual form of a pseudo-random step.

name: reset_state_after_eight_steps
description: Calls eight subroutines, then clears four state words and stores two self-referencing addresses before returning.

name: call_shared_helper_repeatedly
description: Makes a long run of identical calls to one subroutine. The decompiled text is cut off partway through, so the arguments and any later behaviour are not visible.

name: copy_words_reset_state
description: Calls one subroutine, copies two words from fixed source locations into two state words, then clears one state word and sets another to 255 before returning.

name: clear_two_state_words
description: Writes zero to two state words and returns. It has no other logic.

name: store_constant_after_helper_call
description: Calls one subroutine and then stores a fixed constant before returning. The text shown does not contain the longer body the facts describe, and the routine is recorded as writing the background colour register.

name: stub_truncated_decompile
description: The decompiled source stops after its first declarations, so no behaviour is visible. The facts record four subroutine calls and an address-taken entry, but none of those calls appear in the text.

name: register_five_spaced_entries
description: Makes five calls to one setup subroutine, each with an address spaced evenly after the last and the same fixed size and flag arguments, calling a follow-up subroutine after each. The text stops in the middle of a further call.

name: queue_five_entries_mode_b
description: Makes five calls to one setup subroutine with evenly spaced addresses and a different fixed pair of arguments from its neighbours, calling a follow-up subroutine after each. The text stops partway through the last call.

name: register_four_entries_mode_c
description: Makes four calls to one setup subroutine with evenly spaced addresses and a fixed argument pair, then calls a follow-up subroutine and a run of further subroutines. The decompiled text is cut off in the middle.

name: stub_truncated_decompile_b
description: The decompiled source stops after its first declarations, so no behaviour is visible. The facts record a short routine with four subroutine calls, none of which appear in the text.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: advance_byte_cursor_until_end
description: If one flag is clear, calls a subroutine and returns. Otherwise, while a second flag is clear, it reads one byte from a moving cursor and returns unless that byte is the end marker 255. On reaching the marker it sets two words to 255 and two to zero.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_from_table
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for one whose key byte matches a value in a register, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match. It then calls the handler address stored in the entry it stopped on.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_alt_entry
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The code is identical to its neighbour, reached from a different place.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_c
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The decompiled text is the same as the other dispatch routines in this range.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_d
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The decompiled text is the same as the other dispatch routines in this range.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_e
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The decompiled text is the same as the other dispatch routines in this range.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_f
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The facts list more instructions than the shown text contains, but the text is the same dispatch loop.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_g
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The decompiled text is the same as the other dispatch routines in this range.

name: dispatch_keyed_handler_variant_h
description: Scans a table of 10-byte entries for a matching key byte, stopping at a zero-key terminator or the first match, then calls the handler address stored in that entry. The decompiled text matches the other dispatch routines in this range.

name: process_128_slot_flags
description: Walks 128 slots and, for each whose flag byte is set, clears the flag, marks the slot's entry with 255 and calls a subroutine. Slots with a pending entry and a clear secondary byte have the entry cleared and a subroutine called.

name: reset_slot_table_and_pointers
description: Calls a subroutine, clears a 128-entry table, zeroes five handler pointers and two state bytes, then returns.

name: reset_slot_table_with_selector
description: Calls a subroutine, selects one of two candidate handler addresses according to an argument, clears five handler pointers and a 128-entry table, then calls a further subroutine. Several small subroutines are involved but their effects are not shown.

name: scan_eight_bytes_for_one
description: Scans eight bytes of a table and returns early if any byte equals one. If none does, it returns with nothing set, so the routine has no visible result.

name: scan_bytes_offset_two
description: Scans eight bytes starting two bytes into a table and returns early if any byte equals one. Both paths return with nothing set, so the routine has no visible result.

name: acquire_or_release_indexed_slot
description: When its argument is nonzero and the slot is clear, increments each nonzero counter in an 8-entry table and marks the slot set. When the argument is zero, it decrements counters at or above the slot's value and marks the slot clear.

name: acquire_or_release_byte_slot
description: Works like its neighbour on an 8-byte table: nonzero argument increments the nonzero counters when the slot is clear and marks it set, zero argument decrements counters at or above the slot's value and marks it clear.

name: acquire_slot_and_bump_counters
description: If an indexed slot is clear, increments each nonzero counter in a run of bytes before marking the slot set. If the slot is already set, it only marks it set again.

name: initialise_timed_records_table
description: Reads a status value from the joystick and disk port, then fills twelve records from an offset-encoded table, computing each record's rate by dividing a fixed clock constant by a table value. It then fills four further entries with a handler address and a count.

name: reset_disk_and_dma_control
description: Clears a status byte and writes fixed values to the disk-control and DMA registers, finishing by masking one bit off the last value. The facts list the joystick port and the DMA control register.

name: step_four_channel_bytecode
description: Steps four channel records of 40 bytes each. When a channel's counter runs out it reads opcodes from that channel's script: some set a data pointer or a flag, one jumps to another location, and a terminating opcode stops the channel. The routine returns early unless its enable flag and a playing flag are both set. The decompiled text is cut off partway through, so later opcodes are not visible.

name: clear_flag_with_optional_helper
description: Clears a state word and, when a register argument is nonzero, calls a subroutine and stores a second register value into the state word. It then stores a routine address in a global.

name: call_helper_if_state_set
description: Calls a subroutine only if a state word is nonzero, then stores a routine address in a global and returns.

name: call_helper_then_clear_state
description: Calls a subroutine, clears a state word, stores a routine address in a global, and returns a value register.

name: call_helper_with_routine_address
description: Calls one subroutine with a routine address and a zero argument, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: stub_truncated_decompile_c
description: The decompiled text holds only a truncation marker, so the routine's behaviour cannot be recovered from this entry.

name: wait_for_vertical_position_cycle
description: Busy-waits until a raster position value leaves a fixed value, then waits until it returns to that value. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: call_helper_then_wait_position
description: Calls one subroutine, then runs the same two-stage wait on the raster position value as its neighbour, returning once the value reaches the fixed value.

name: call_helper_routine_address_b
description: Calls one subroutine with a routine address and a zero argument, then returns. It has no other logic and matches a neighbouring routine.

name: stub_truncated_decompile_d
description: The decompiled text holds only a truncation marker, so the routine's behaviour cannot be recovered from this entry.

name: stub_truncated_decompile_e
description: The decompiled text holds only a truncation marker, so the routine's behaviour cannot be recovered from this entry. The facts record one subroutine call.

name: call_list_entries_return_last
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of two-word entries, calling a subroutine for each one, and returns the last subroutine result. Does nothing if the list pointer is null.

name: call_list_return_last_b
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of two-word entries, calling a subroutine for each one, and returns the last subroutine result. Does nothing if the list pointer is null. The code matches its neighbours.

name: call_list_return_last_c
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of two-word entries, calling a subroutine for each one, and returns the last subroutine result. Does nothing if the list pointer is null. The code matches its neighbours.

name: call_list_return_last_d
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of two-word entries, calling a subroutine for each one, and returns the last subroutine result. Does nothing if the list pointer is null. The code matches its neighbours.

name: call_each_list_entry_void
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of two-word entries and calls a subroutine for each one. Returns nothing and does nothing if the list pointer is null.

name: clear_buffer_walk_byte_blocks
description: Clears a 320-byte buffer, then walks a zero-terminated byte sequence in blocks of eight, calling a subroutine for each non-zero position in turn and stopping at a zero byte. It then stores 319 and 7 into the buffer header and calls a subroutine.

name: merge_shifted_record_into_rows
description: Loads a 16-byte record into four shared longwords, shifting them right by a count or copying them unchanged when the count is zero. It then ORs two mask bytes into each of seven rows of a buffer that are 40 bytes apart.

name: setup_blitter_for_clipped_copy
description: Checks that a horizontal position and width fit within a 320-pixel line, clipping the start when it is negative and returning minus one when the region is out of range. It waits for the blitter to be idle, then sets its first-word masks, modulo, control and size registers for the copy.

name: setup_entry_after_checked_call
description: Calls a subroutine and returns its failure value when that is minus one. Otherwise, if a target word is zero, it writes two fields of an entry, calls five subroutines and returns zero.

name: queue_blitter_request_fields
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then stores a source address, either a default value or a supplied value depending on a flag bit, a second value and a size word into the request record.

name: return_byte_argument_unchanged
description: Returns its byte argument unchanged. Several callers use it as an identity function.

name: decrement_counter_call_at_zero
description: Decrements a counter stored in a record and calls a subroutine when it reaches zero. Otherwise it returns.

name: return_immediately_stub_b
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: poll_state_and_set_flag
description: When a state byte is clear, calls a subroutine and, if it reports a nonzero value, clears a flag and sets the state byte to one. When the state byte is set, it sets the flag, writes 253 and minus one into state words and returns.

name: decrement_counter_then_compare_call
description: Calls a subroutine and decrements a counter in a record. When the counter reaches zero and a stored value differs by one from a table entry, it calls a further subroutine.

name: return_immediately_stub_c
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: check_byte_below_nine_max
description: When a flag is clear, calls a subroutine and returns if the byte argument is below nine. Otherwise it stores 255 in a state word.

name: run_entry_update_loop
description: Calls an indirect routine from a record, then loops indefinitely over records: for each record whose state is not two it calls subroutines, with an extra subroutine when a flag bit is set. It then calls a subroutine and clears a byte in the record.

name: copy_rectangle_between_regions
description: Copies a rectangular block of words between two regions of a screen buffer. The block size and source and destination offsets come from fields of a record, and each row is copied with the destination stepped by a fixed row stride.

name: compute_shape_bounds_from_records
description: Initialises four bound values to sentinels, then walks a list of shape records, updating the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical extents from each record and calling subroutines per record. The decompiled text stops partway through.

name: expand_bytes_through_lookup_table
description: Fills a buffer with rows whose width and count come from a record, copying each source byte through a lookup table into the destination, then stores the end pointer back into the record.

name: lookup_scaled_offset_by_index
description: For index zero, returns a record field shifted left by four. Otherwise it looks up a table entry by index minus one and returns it shifted left by five.

name: randomise_offset_and_trigger_effect
description: Stores an index and a counter from a record and, when a flag byte is set, draws two five-bit random offsets from a subroutine. It applies a sign to one offset, adds both to a global, then calls another subroutine with a record-derived object, 100 and 1.

name: or_fixed_mask_into_value
description: Returns its argument with a fixed bit pattern ORed in. The mask sets several high bits.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes. Where two boxes overlap it calls subroutines chosen by each object's type code, and sets a state byte to two for certain type pairs. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_b
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_c
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_d
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_g
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_h
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_i
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_j
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_pairs_k
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes, calling subroutines chosen by type code where they overlap. The routine shares its code with several entry points.

name: test_box_overlap_with_calls
description: Tests pairs of objects from two nested lists for overlap of their bounding boxes. Where two boxes overlap it calls several subroutines and sets a state byte, and the decompiled text stops partway through.

name: set_object_byte_from_record
description: Stores a byte in an object, computed from a record value shifted right by two, adding three when a global flag is clear. It then sets bit zero of the object's flag byte.

name: compute_object_anchor_and_extents
description: Derives an anchor address for an object from either a record offset or a table entry, then computes a position and two extents from record fields and stores them in shared globals.

name: compute_extents_call_if_visible
description: Derives an anchor and extents for an object in the same way as its neighbour, then calls a subroutine only when the object's horizontal and vertical extents fall inside the supplied bounds.

name: scan_rows_for_bounding_overlap
description: Scans a range of rows, testing on each row whether two stored extents overlap, and stops at the first row where they do. The result is left in shared state rather than returned.

name: walk_record_list_with_callback
description: Clears shared state, then walks a list of records. For each record it calls subroutines, copies sixteen words of state and calls a callback address depending on flags. The decompiled text stops partway through.

name: no_op_pointer_check
description: Compares a pointer with two addresses, discards the result and returns. It has no effect.

name: call_helper_then_store_argument
description: Calls a subroutine and, if a flag stays clear, zeroes a state word, stores a register argument in a global and calls a further subroutine.

name: load_record_list_into_context
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of pointers to records, copying each record's fields into a context block, calling a subroutine and then processing that record's sub-list. It returns when the list ends. The decompiled text is cut off partway through.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decoded bytes are not valid instructions. The routine is one unresolved call followed by a bad-instruction halt, so there is no behaviour to describe.

name: merge_changed_bits_into_accumulator
description: Over a 128-byte block, ORs into an accumulator the bits of a new block that differ from the previously saved block, then saves the new block as the previous one. Two state words are updated the same way.

name: clear_three_128_byte_tables
description: Zeroes three 128-byte tables in turn, one longword at a time.

name: link_nineteen_nodes_in_sequence
description: Chains nineteen entries together by storing in each the address 118 bytes beyond it, terminates the last with zero, then sets two head pointers to a fixed address.

name: xor_fold_words_masked
description: XORs together a run of longwords from a buffer and returns the result masked to every other bit. It works like a simple checksum fold.

name: return_immediately_stub_d
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_e
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_f
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller. One routine calls it.

name: set_handler_call_five_steps
description: Stores a routine address in a shared global, then calls five subroutines in sequence.

name: step_counter_toward_target
description: Steps a shared counter one unit at a time toward a target address, calling subroutines at each step, while a status bit stays set. When the loop ends it sets a second counter to minus eight.

name: step_counter_on_status_poll
description: Steps a shared counter toward a target address in a loop that re-checks a status bit each pass. The register note records that this port holds the joystick fire buttons and disk status. When the bit clears it sets a second counter to minus eight and returns.

name: set_counter_to_minus_eight
description: Sets a shared counter to minus eight and returns.

name: return_immediately_stub_g
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_h
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_i
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_j
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: start_disk_read_sync_word
description: If a flag is set, records a timeout error and returns. Otherwise it programs disk registers with a sync word, a DMA pointer and a length, then polls a status bit for up to 201 passes. It returns with a timeout error if the status bit never completes.

name: start_disk_read_polling_status
description: Programs the same disk registers and sync word as its neighbour, then polls a status bit for up to 201 passes. It returns on completion or records a timeout error when the bit never sets.

name: set_control_field_constant
description: Writes a fixed constant into one field of a control record and returns.

name: poll_flag_table_clear_b
description: Its opening test is always true, so it returns without doing anything and the wait-and-clear logic after it is unreachable as written. It is the same routine as its neighbour.

name: stub_bad_instruction_tail
description: Calls several subroutines and then reaches a bad-instruction halt in the decompiled text, so the behaviour after the arithmetic is not recoverable.

name: return_immediately_stub_k
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_l
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: return_immediately_stub_m
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.
